title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 159
paragraphs: During the lifetime of the first settler Battus, who reigned forty years, and of his son Arcesilaus, who reigned sixteen years, the Cyrenaeans continued to live there with the same numbers they had brought when they first set out for the colony; but in the time of the third king, called Battus the Fortunate, the Pythian priestess gave an oracle urging the Hellenes in general to sail and join the Cyrenaeans in settling Libya—for the Cyrenaeans were inviting them, with the promise of a division of land. The oracle she uttered was this:
“Whoever goes to the much-desired land, to Libya, after the land has been divided—I say he shall one day regret it.”

So great numbers gathered at Cyrene, and the Libyans who lived round about had much land cut away from their possessions. Therefore they, with their king whose name was Adicran—being deprived not only of their country but also treated with great insolence by the Cyrenaeans—sent to Egypt and gave themselves up to Apries, king of Egypt. He gathered a great army of Egyptians and sent it against Cyrene; but the Cyrenaeans marched out to the region of Irasa and the spring Theste, and there joined battle with the Egyptians and defeated them. For the Egyptians had not before tried the Hellenes in battle and so despised them, and they were slaughtered to the point that only a few returned back to Egypt. Because of this, and because they laid the blame on Apries, the Egyptians revolted against him.
